status: hypothetical-teaching-model; inventory accounting only, not an empirical comparative LCA
numericProvenanceDefault: All products, quantities, prices, emissions, feasible activities, reference technologies and use scenarios are invented. Source arguments motivate distinctions; no source supplies these data or endorses a universal method.
inventoryRows: fossil CO2 emitted to air, kg

activityBasis.joint: one indivisible stipulated batch yielding 4 kg X and 6 kg Y in fixed proportions
activityBasis.standaloneX: one operation supplies 1 kg functionally equivalent X
activityBasis.standaloneY: one operation supplies 1 kg functionally equivalent Y
activityBasis.wasteY: one operation treats 1 kg unused joint Y without recovery

partitionQuestion: How shall the inventory of one existing fully saleable batch be assigned to product labels under an expressly chosen mass or gross-sales convention? No production response is estimated.
partitionScope: q=1 only; all common burdens in joint inventory, no separable product-specific burdens. Fractions apply flow by flow. Nonnegative shares sum to one.
decisionQuestion: For one bounded service basket of 4 kg X and 6 kg Y delivered at the specified recipient gate and period, replace independent supply with one joint batch, topping up Y and treating unused joint Y if necessary. What is the conditional change in each inventory flow?
qMeaning: Scenario-stipulated fraction of joint Y that reaches the specified existing Y service; every utilized kg replaces exactly one kg of the stated standalone Y supply. Remaining joint Y is treated as waste; missing Y service is supplied separately. q is not a free credit multiplier or an inferred price response.

assessment.interpretation: Two inventory coordinates retain their distinct units. No LCIA, cross-flow total, damage assessment or whole-environment ranking is performed.

residualInterpretation: An X-anchored comparison residual is a subtraction of the named reference supply, not a physical route inventory, atmospheric removal, intrinsic product property or simultaneous additive assignment to both co-products. Standalone Y top-up remains in the direct route and cancels only when deriving the reduced residual.
premises: X and Y are different specified material services; their equal mass unit does not make them interchangeable.
The joint process cannot vary one valuable output independently; reference technologies are stipulated independent alternatives.

Inventory coefficients describe complete included burdens of their named operations, with no overlap between joint, top-up and treatment inventories. All other activities and elementary flows are omitted, not empirically zero.
Only the enumerated bounded activity changes are asserted. Unchanged capital burdens are outside this operating comparison; no plant-construction or investment claim is made.

The recipients' X and Y requirements are fixed. Useful joint Y substitutes 1:1 in quality, location, timing and downstream use; no further processing or downstream differences are stipulated in this toy case.

Alternative supply can decrease by the indicated quantities and joint operation can replace the stated X supply; no constraints, market price feedback, rebound, delayed response or other induced activities are modeled.
Actual supplier response and q require evidence before real-world interpretation; observed sales prices or a sale alone do not verify displacement.
CU prices only determine the illustrative full-use accounting shares, not the decision activities or who determines joint output.
All emissions are positive physical flows in each actual route. A negative residual is a reference subtraction; it is not atmospheric removal, negative physical production or a product property.
No LCIA factors or cross-flow aggregation are used. CO2 and SO2 comparisons remain separate and imply no total environmental ranking.
Partial-use scenarios are separately changed service-delivery conditions, not applications of Weidema's rules or his corrected examples.
